claims.claim_text: The indexed Captain Lawrence Hollander is Lawrence L. Hollander, the Chicago lawyer and amateur radio operator recruited and commissioned by the OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact first and last name, matching captain grade, Chicago radio specialty, Area C assignment, and same Box 342 context align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on exact name, matching commissioned grade, distinctive occupation and radio specialty, and specific OSS communications assignment.
claims.temporal_assessment: The NPS study explicitly places the lawyer occupation at recruitment and his Area C assignment in early 1943.
claims.match_notes: The adjacent L. L. Hollander row may be a rank-progression duplicate, but the two rows and people remain separate pending Box 342 review.

claims.claim_text: Hollander was a lawyer in Chicago immediately before OSS recruitment.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The NPS study directly identifies the occupation and city at the moment of recruitment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name, captain-grade, and Area C match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly immediate, but the source does not name a firm, employer, or practice arrangement.
claims.match_notes: No reliable named pre-OSS employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed. Private practice is not inferred.

claims.claim_text: The indexed L. L. Hollander may be the same person as the adjacent Captain Lawrence Hollander row, but the identity remains unresolved.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The matching initials, adjacent position, shared box and location, and compatible lieutenant-to-captain progression support a possible duplicate; no service number or direct file linkage establishes it.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Ambiguous. The evidence is stronger than a name-only match but does not meet the project's identity standard.
claims.temporal_assessment: The rank sequence is compatible with promotion, but the index provides no dates.
claims.match_notes: This candidate remains private review evidence. The source row retains its own person ID and archival profile.

claims.claim_text: If the two Hollander rows represent one person, the L. L. row may also belong to the Chicago lawyer documented by NPS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The occupation is documented for Lawrence L. Hollander but has not been directly linked to the initials-only row.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Ambiguous and below the publication threshold.
claims.temporal_assessment: Potentially immediate only if the duplicate hypothesis is confirmed.
claims.match_notes: No employer or occupation is published as fact for the L. L. row.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Marvin S. Flisser is the Brooklyn College graduate and OSS communications trainee documented by the National Park Service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact full name, middle initial, private status, Bronx origin, Area C communications training, and winter 1943-1944 chronology align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on exact rare name plus rank, hometown, training specialty, location, and dates.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS places Brooklyn College graduation before winter 1943-1944 Area C training.
claims.match_notes: Box 240 remains unreviewed. The full service number is excluded from public output.

claims.claim_text: Flisser was a Brooklyn College graduate before his OSS communications training.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official history explicitly identifies Brooklyn College graduation and then dates his Area C training to winter 1943-1944.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the rare exact-name and communications-training match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented pre-OSS education; it is not established as the immediate predecessor to recruitment.
claims.match_notes: Brooklyn College is classified as student status, not an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Willis S. Georgia Jr. is W. Scudder Georgia Jr., the naval radio instructor recruited into OSS communications work.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The surname, first initial expansion, Scudder middle name, suffix, radio expertise, Chicago recruitment, and overseas OSS communications service align across NPS and a reputable obituary.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the unusual surname-suffix combination and multiple matching military, technical, and OSS identifiers.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS dates the Navy-to-OSS recruitment to 1943; the obituary independently places Hobart attendance before OSS recruitment.
claims.match_notes: Box 268 remains unreviewed. Postwar career and family details were not used as pre-OSS evidence.

claims.claim_text: Georgia's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was commissioned service in the United States Navy as a radio instructor in Chicago.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS directly describes Georgia and two colleagues as new naval officers and radio instructors when an OSS communications recruiter enlisted them.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the distinctive name, suffix, radio specialty, and OSS communications match.
claims.match_notes: This is a military assignment, not a civilian employer. The specific Navy school or unit is not named.

claims.claim_text: Georgia attended Hobart College before OSS recruitment.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Washington Post obituary explicitly sequences Hobart attendance before his wartime OSS recruitment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence after corroboration with the exact suffix, communications specialty, and NPS recruitment account.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented pre-OSS education; exact attendance dates are not stated.
claims.match_notes: Hobart College is student status and is not classified as an employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Robert R. Kehoe is the New Jersey Signal Corps radio trainee and OSS Jedburgh radioman who authored the CIA-hosted memoir.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact full name, middle initial, New Jersey origin, age, Signal Corps radio training, Area B experience, and unique Jedburgh communications role align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on exact name and a dense set of consistent military, technical, geographic, age, training, and mission identifiers.
claims.temporal_assessment: The first-person memoir dates Signal Corps enlistment to September 1942 and sequences selection into OSS after Camp Crowder training.
claims.match_notes: Box 396 remains unreviewed. The full service number is never shown publicly.

claims.claim_text: Kehoe's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was enlisted service and radio training in the United States Army Signal Corps.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Kehoe's memoir traces his Signal Corps enlistment and Camp Crowder training directly into volunteer selection and discovery in Washington that the group belonged to OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name and first-person chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly immediate; the memoir supplies a continuous Signal Corps-to-OSS sequence.
claims.match_notes: The Signal Corps is a military assignment and is not labeled a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Kehoe's last documented civilian work before military service was laboratory work at an unnamed chemical plant.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Kehoe states that he worked at a chemical plant at age 19 and then enlisted in the Army Signal Corps in September 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name, age, and first-person service chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded before Signal Corps enlistment; the employer name and exact separation date are not supplied.
claims.match_notes: The occupation is documented, but no reliable named civilian employer has yet been identified. No chemical company is inferred.
